examples.dm: It is not for the sake of the increase, decrease, or grasping of form; Nor is it for the sake of grasping the various phenomena that one trains. While training, one also grasps omniscience itself; This very transcendence is the training of those who delight in excellence.
examples.gm: It is not for the sake of the increase, complete deterioration, or complete apprehension of form; Not training for the sake of completely apprehending various dharmas, Yet training and completely apprehending omniscience itself— Whatever definite emergence this is, this is the training that rejoices in qualities.
examples.sa: न च रुपवृद्धिपरिहाणिपरिग्रहाये न च शिक्षति विविधधर्मपरिग्रहाये । सर्वज्ञतां च परिगृह्णति शिक्षमाणो निर्यायती य इय शिक्ष गुणे रतानाम् ॥

examples.dm: Just as seeds that are sown and remain in the earth will eventually grow, Once the assembly of conditions is found, diverse forms are fully produced; The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them are born from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Seeds, having been sown and resting in the earth, will arise; Having found the proper conditions, many kinds of forms are fully produced. The five perfections and however many qualities of awakening there are, All of them also are produced from the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: बीजाः प्रकीर्ण पृथिवीस्थित संभवन्ति सामग्रि लब्ध्व विरुहन्ति अनेकरुपाः । यावन्ति बोधिगुण पारमिताश् च पञ्च प्रज्ञाय पारमित ते विरुहन्ति सर्वे ॥

examples.dm: Just as when the solar orb radiates its web of light, Sentient beings then apply themselves diligently to their tasks, So too, when the mind of enlightenment arises in the world for the sake of the wisdom of the sages, Through primordial wisdom, sentient beings come to possess the qualities of the Dharma.
examples.gm: When the sun's disk emits its web of light, At that time beings exert themselves in doing their work; likewise, When the mind of awakening emerges in the world for the sake of the knowledge of the wise, Through pristine knowledge beings become endowed with virtuous dharmas.
examples.sa: आदित्यमण्डलु यदा प्रभजाल मुञ्ची कर्मक्रियासु तद सत्त्व पराक्रमन्ति । तथ बोधिचित्त सद लोकविदुस्य ज्ञातो ज्ञानेन सर्वगुणधर्म समागमन्ति ॥

examples.dm: Those who think, "May I become a disciple of the Sugata," And those who desire to become Pratyekabuddhas or likewise Kings of Dharma, Cannot achieve these without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot cross from this shore to the other without seeing the ferry.
examples.gm: Whoever thinks they will become a śrāvaka of the Sugata, Or a pratyekabuddha, and likewise wishes to become a Dharma King, Cannot attain it without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot see a crossing to go from this shore to the other.
examples.sa: यो इच्छती सुगतश्रावक हं भवेयं प्रत्येकबुद्ध भवियां तथ धर्मराजो । इमु क्षान्त्यनागमि न शक्यति प्रापुणेतुं यथ आरपारगमनाय अतीतदर्शी ॥

examples.dm: Why is that? Because those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Here demonstrate that all phenomena are emptiness. Having heard that, the Hearers quickly reach liberation, And they reach the awakening of Pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of Buddhas.
examples.gm: If asked why: those supreme speakers, having trained in this, Demonstrate all dharmas here as emptiness. Hearing that, śrāvakas swiftly touch complete liberation, And touch the awakening of pratyekabuddhas and the awakening of buddhas.
examples.sa: किं कारणं त इह शिक्षित वादिश्रेष्ठा गमयन्ति धर्म निखिलानिह शून्यतायाम् । यां श्रुत्व श्रावक स्पृशन्ति विमुक्ति शीघ्रं प्रत्येकबोधि स्पृशयन्ति च बुद्धबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: However much the hosts of śrāvakas generate a mass of merit Through being endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, It cannot match even a fraction of a bodhisattva’s single thought of rejoicing; The mass of merit of the śrāvaka hosts cannot match even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Even if however many hosts of śrāvakas generate collections of merit, Fully endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, Compared to a single mind of rejoicing of a bodhisattva, The heap of merit of the hosts of śrāvakas cannot match it.
examples.sa: यावन्ति श्रावकगणाः प्रसवन्ति पुण्यं दानं च शीलमपि भावनसंप्रयुक्तम् । स हि बोधिसत्त्व अनुमोदन एकचित्ते न च सर्वश्रावकगणे सिय पुण्यस्कन्धो ॥

examples.dm: Just as a wandering mendicant, through his knowledge of craftsmanship, Brings about the disintegration of the aggregates without any objective apprehension, Any bodhisattva who understands phenomena in that way, Does not touch nirvana, and is established in wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as the wanderer Śreṇika, through his knowledge, Understood the aggregates as unapprehendable and subject to destruction; Whatever bodhisattva understands phenomena in that way Does not contact nirvāṇa, and dwells in wisdom.
examples.sa: अथ श्रेणिकस्य अभुती परिव्राजकस्य ज्ञानोपलम्भु न हि स्कन्धविभावना च । यो बोधिसत्त्व परिजानति एव धर्मां न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति सो विहराति प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: The fourth chapter explains the complete realization of all aspects. Śakra, the king of the gods, asked the Victor: "How do Bodhisattvas practicing wisdom apply diligence?" "They do not apply even a particle of diligence toward the aggregates or the elements; Not applying diligence toward the aggregates is the Bodhisattva's diligence."
examples.gm: The fourth chapter: teaching the complete realization of all aspects. The king of gods, Śakra, asked the Victor: "How does a bodhisattva strive in the practice of wisdom?" "They do not strive even a speck of dust in the aggregates and elements; Not striving in the aggregates, that is the striving of a bodhisattva."
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनस्य परिपृच्छति देवराजो चरमाण प्रज्ञ कथ युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । अणुमात्र यो न खलु युज्यति स्कन्धधातौ यो एव युज्यति स युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वः ॥

examples.dm: Those of great renown don the armor of difficult deeds, Which is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, and sense sources. They are free from the concept of the three vehicles and have no grasping; They are irreversible, unwavering, and possess the quality of being imperturbable.
examples.gm: Those endowed with great renown don the armor that is difficult to do; It is not the armor of the aggregates, elements, or sense bases. They are free from the perception of the three vehicles and have no grasping. They are irreversible, unwavering, and of unperturbed nature.
examples.sa: संनाहु दुष्करू महायशु संनहन्ती न च स्कन्धधातु न च आयतनैः सनद्धाः । त्रिभि यानसंज्ञविगता अपरिगृहीता अविवर्तिका अचलिताश्च अकोप्यधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Whatever Dharma the Victor’s Śrāvakas may teach, Explain, or express through logical reasoning, And whatever attainment of supreme, noble bliss and its fruits they achieve, All of these are the power of the Tathāgata, the Great Being.
examples.gm: However much the śrāvakas of the Jina teach the Dharma, Explaining and expressing it logically, Creating supreme noble bliss and attaining its results, All of that is the power of the person of the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: यावन्ति धर्म जिनश्रावक देशयन्ति भाषन्ति युक्तिसहितांश् च उदीरयन्ति । परमार्थसौख्यक्रिय तत्फलप्राप्तिता च सर्वो अयं पुरुषकारु तथागतस्य ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who abides here in peace in this way, Has been prophesied by the Tathāgatas of the past. They have no conceit of thinking, "I am in meditative equipoise," or "I have arisen," Why is that? Because the nature of phenomena is fully understood.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva dwells here thus in peace, Is prophesied by the Tathāgatas of the past. They have no conceited thought, "I am in meditative equipoise" or "I have arisen." Why is this? Because they completely understand the nature of phenomena.
examples.sa: एवात्मशान्ति विहरन्निह बोधिसत्त्वो सो व्याकृतो पुरमकेहि तथागतेहि । न च मन्यते अहु समाधितु व्युत्थितो वा कस्मार्थ धर्मप्रकृतिं परिजानयित्वा ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: The bodhisattva does not apprehend a prior limit, a later limit, Or a present; they are the purity of the three times. That which is such is unconditioned and free from conceptual elaboration; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Bodhisattvas do not apprehend the past limit, the future limit, And the present occurrence; the three times are pure. They are unconditioned and free from conceptual proliferation; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: पूर्वान्ततो न उपलभ्यति बोधिसत्त्वो अपरान्ततोऽपि प्रतिउपन्न त्रियध्वशुद्धो । यो शुद्ध सो अनभिसंस्कृतु निष्प्रपञ्चो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Just as the Guide does not dwell in the unconditioned realm, Likewise, one does not dwell in the conditioned, but practices without a fixed location; In that way, the bodhisattva dwells by not dwelling in any basis; To dwell without a location is what the Victor has taught as "dwelling."
examples.gm: Just as the Guide does not abide in the unconditioned realm, Likewise not abiding in the conditioned, practicing without abiding; Thus the bodhisattva abides in an abiding that is without abiding; Abiding without abiding, this is taught as abiding by the Victorious One.
examples.sa: यथ नायकोऽस्थितकु धातुअसंस्कृताया तथ संस्कृताय अथितो अनिकेतचारी । एवं च स्थानु अथितो स्थित बोधिसत्त्वो अस्थानु स्थानु अयु स्थानु जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Those who engage in the practice of benefit and compassion, Having trained in this vidyā-mantra, the wise shall touch enlightenment; One should know that all forms of happiness, Whether conditioned or unconditioned, arise from this.
examples.gm: Those who practice the practices endowed with benefit and compassion, The wise ones, having trained in this mantra, will touch awakening. Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness, One should know that all those forms of happiness arise from this.
examples.sa: ये वा चरन्ति चरियां हितसानुकम्पाम् इह विद्यशिक्षित विदु स्पृशिष्यन्ति बोधिम् । ये सौख्य संस्कृत असंस्कृत ये च सौख्या सर्वे च सौख्य प्रसुता इतु वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, if you wish to attain the supreme primordial wisdom of a Buddha, Have faith in this Mother of the Victors. For example, it would be unfitting to be like a merchant who, Having traveled to an island of jewels, returns home with his goods exhausted.
examples.gm: Therefore, if the supreme pristine wisdom of a buddha One wishes to touch, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! For example, having gone to the island of jewels, a merchant Returning bereft of goods—it is not fitting to become like that.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु श्रद्दधत एव जिनान मातां यदि इच्छथा स्पृशितु उत्तमबुद्धज्ञानम् । सो वाणिजो यथ व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं मूलातु छेदन करित्व पुन आगमेया ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, although a bodhisattva may possess great faith, If they lack wisdom, they will quickly deteriorate. When faith is fully embraced by wisdom, They will transcend the two levels and attain supreme awakening.
examples.gm: Likewise, although a bodhisattva may have much faith, If they are completely lacking in wisdom, they will quickly become unfit. If their faith is fully embraced by wisdom, Having entirely transcended the two grounds, they will attain supreme enlightenment.
examples.sa: किंचापि श्रद्धबहुलो सिय बोधिसत्त्वो प्रज्ञाविहीन विलयं लघु प्रापुणाति । तं चैव श्रद्ध परिगृह्णयमान प्रज्ञा अतिक्रम्य बोधिद्वय प्राप्स्यति अग्रबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: In which form is not apprehended, nor feeling, nor perception, Nor consciousness, nor intention is apprehended, And all phenomena are thoroughly known to be unborn and empty— This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Where form is not, feeling is not, and perception is not apprehended, Consciousness is not, and volition is not apprehended, And all dharmas are fully known in the manner of being unarisen and empty: This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यस्मिन् न रूप अपि वेदन चापि संज्ञा विज्ञान नैव न पि चेतनयोपलब्धिः । अनुपादु शून्य न य जानति सर्वधर्मान् एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: When conditioned and unconditioned phenomena, as well as white and black dharmas, Have been thoroughly deconstructed by wisdom so that not even an atom is observed, That is accounted as the perfection of wisdom in the world; It is just like space, which does not abide in anything at all.
examples.gm: When conditioned, unconditioned, and white and black dharmas Are broken down by wisdom and not even a particle is apprehended, In the world it is reckoned as the perfection of wisdom; It is like space, which does not abide anywhere at all.
examples.sa: यद धर्म संस्कृत असंस्कृत कृष्णशुक्लो अणुमात्रु नो लभति प्रज्ञ विभावमानः । यद प्रज्ञपारमित गच्छति संख्य लोके आकाश यत्र न प्रतिष्ठितु किंचि तत्र ॥

examples.dm: When a bodhisattva, through the perfection of wisdom, sees That all phenomena are naturally pure and utterly pristine, They do not perceive an agent, nor do they perceive any phenomena; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: All dharmas being naturally pure and entirely pure, If the bodhisattva views the perfection of wisdom, Not apprehending an agent and not apprehending all dharmas, This is practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: प्रकृतीय शुद्ध परिशुद्धिमि सर्वधर्मां प्रज्ञाय पारमित पश्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । न च पश्यकं लभति नापि च सर्वधर्मान् एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Those who have entered into the supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoice from the depths of their hearts in the generation of the mind of enlightenment; Though one might find the measure of the three thousandfold world system and Mount Meru by weighing them on a scale, The virtue of such rejoicing is not like that.
examples.gm: Regarding those who have fully entered supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoicing from the depths of one's heart in their generation of the mind— The Mount Meru of a trichiliocosm could be measured by weighing it on a scale, But the virtue of that rejoicing is not like that.
examples.sa: अविवर्तियस्य वरबोधयि प्रस्थितस्य यो चित्तुपादु अनुमोदितु आशयेन । त्रिसहस्र मेरु तुलयित्व सियाप्रमाणो न त्वेव तस्य कुशलस्यनुमोदनाये ॥

examples.dm: I also rejoice in the mass of merit of all sentient beings, as many as there are, Who strive for virtue and desire to be of benefit; Therefore, once they have attained the qualities of the Victors, They bestow the gift of Dharma upon the world in order to bring suffering to an end.
examples.gm: Seeking virtue and desiring to benefit however many sentient beings there are, They also rejoice in the heaps of merit of them all; Therefore, having attained the qualities of the Victorious Ones, In order to exhaust suffering, they give the gift of Dharma to the world.
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व कुशलार्थिक मोक्षकामा सर्वेष भोन्ति अनुमोदितु पुण्यराशि । सत्त्वर्थि ते जिनगुण अनन्त प्रापुणित्वा दास्यन्ति धर्म जगती दुखसंक्षयाये ॥

examples.dm: Yet a wise bodhisattva with skillful means Were to rejoice in the substance of those meritorious deeds, And fully dedicate it toward supreme, sublime enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings, By that complete dedication, one will outshine all living beings.
examples.gm: Whatever wise bodhisattva, skilled in means, Rejoices in their bases of meritorious actions, And fully dedicates them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings, By fully dedicating them, they outshine all beings.
examples.sa: यश् चो उपायकुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो तेषां स पुण्यक्रियवस्त्वनुमोदयित्वा । सत्त्वार्थ अग्रवरबोधयि नामयेया अभिभोति सर्वजगती परिणामयुक्तो ॥

examples.dm: In the same way, these five perfections of the Victors Also acquire the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When they are fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, known as "awakening."
examples.gm: Likewise, these five perfections of the Victors also Will attain the very name of the perfection of wisdom. When fully dedicated for the sake of omniscience, All these six become of one taste, called awakening.
examples.sa: एमेव पञ्च इमि पारमिता जिनानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित नामतया भवन्ति । सर्वज्ञताय परिणामयमाण सर्वे षडपीह एकनयम् अर्छति बोधिनामा ॥

examples.dm: If one understands that these phenomena have ceased and are exhausted, And that which is dedicated is also exhausted, And that a phenomenon never dedicates to a phenomenon, Then by knowing in such a way, it is a perfect dedication.
examples.gm: If in this way one knows that this dharma has ceased and is exhausted, And that to which it is dedicated is also exhausted, And knows that a dharma is never dedicated to a dharma, Through knowing in that way, it is perfectly dedicated.
examples.sa: सचि एव जानति निरुध्यति क्षीणधर्मा तच्चैत क्षीण परिणामयिष्यन्ति यत्र । न च धर्म धर्मि परिणामयते कदाचित् परिणामितं भवति एव प्रजानमाने ॥

examples.dm: Yet a wise bodhisattva with skillful means Were to rejoice in the substance of those meritorious deeds, And fully dedicate it toward supreme, sublime enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings, By that complete dedication, one will outshine all living beings.
examples.gm: Whatever wise bodhisattva, skilled in means, Rejoices in their bases of meritorious actions, And fully dedicates them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings, By fully dedicating them, they outshine all beings.
examples.sa: यश् चो उपायकुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो तेषां स पुण्यक्रियवस्त्वनुमोदयित्वा । सत्त्वार्थ अग्रवरबोधयि नामयेया अभिभोति सर्वजगती परिणामयुक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Supreme enlightenment is not reached by the initial mind, Yet without that initial mind, it cannot be reached. Peaceful enlightenment is not attained by the final mind, Yet without that, it is also impossible to attain it.
examples.gm: By the first mind, supreme awakening is not touched, Yet without it, one is not able to touch it. By the final mind, peaceful awakening is not attained, Yet without it, one is not able to attain it.
examples.sa: प्रथमेव चित्त स्पृशती न च अग्रबोधिम् असता न तस्य स्पृशता पुन शक्य भोन्ति । न च चित्त पश्चिम शिवाम् अनुप्रापुणाति असता न तस्य पुन प्रापणनाय शक्यम् ॥

examples.dm: From a seed, the sprout, flower, and fruit arise; Just as it is not the case that the tree does not exist because the seed has ceased, So too, the initial mind is the cause of awakening; It is not the case that awakening does not exist because that mind has ceased.
examples.gm: From a seed, a sprout, a flower, and a fruit arise, And when it ceases, the tree is not absent there—just as, Likewise, the first mind is also the cause of awakening, And when it ceases, it is not that awakening is absent.
examples.sa: बीजातु स्तम्ब फल पुष्प समागमन्ति सो वानिरुद्ध असतो न हि तस्य वृक्षो । एमेव चित्त प्रथमं तु निदान बोधेः सो वा निरुद्ध असतो न हि तस्य बोधिः ॥

examples.dm: Just as a water jar is gradually filled from the first drop to the last, Little by little, it is completely filled; So too, the initial mind is the cause of supreme enlightenment, And by gradually perfecting virtuous qualities, one becomes a Buddha.
examples.gm: By drops of water, a vase from the first to the last, Is gradually, little by little, fully filled—just as, Likewise, the first mind too is the cause of supreme awakening, Gradually, perfecting white virtues, one becomes a buddha.
examples.sa: उदकबिन्दु कुम्भ परिपूर्यति स्तोकस्तोकं प्रथमे निपाति अनुपूर्व स पश्चिमेन । एमेव चित्त प्रथमं वरबोधिहेतुर् अनुपूर्व शुक्लगुणपूर्ण भवन्ति बुद्धाः ॥

examples.dm: In the language of India: Ārya-prajñāpāramitā-sañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: 'Phags pa shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa sdud pa tshigs su bcad pa. Homage to the Noble Mañjuśrī!
examples.gm: In the language of India: Āryaprajñāpāramitāsañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: The Noble Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom. Homage to the noble Mañjuśrī.
examples.sa: ओम् नमो भगवत्यै आर्यप्रज्ञापारमितारत्नगुणसंचयगाथायै । नमो आर्यमञ्जुश्रिये ।

examples.dm: May the Noble Verses Summarizing the Perfection of Wisdom be complete.
examples.gm: The Noble Verses on the Collection of the Perfection of Wisdom is complete.
examples.sa: आर्याष्टसाहस्रिकाया भगवत्याः प्रज्ञापारमितायाः परिवर्तानुसारेण भगवती रत्नगुणसंचयगाथा समाप्ता ॥

examples.dm: Those who think, "May I become a disciple of the Sugata," And those who desire to become Pratyekabuddhas or likewise Kings of Dharma, Cannot achieve these without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot cross from this shore to the other without seeing the ferry.
examples.gm: Whoever thinks they will become a śrāvaka of the Sugata, Or a pratyekabuddha, and likewise wishes to become a Dharma King, Cannot attain it without relying on this patience, Just as one cannot see a crossing to go from this shore to the other.
examples.sa: यो इच्छती सुगतश्रावक हं भवेयं प्रत्येकबुद्ध भवियां तथ धर्मराजो । इमु क्षान्त्यनागमि न शक्यति प्रापुणेतुं यथ आरपारगमनाय अतीतदर्शी ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as the rays of the sun abiding in the sky Dry up the earth and make forms clearly visible, Likewise, the Dharma King, relying on the Perfection of Wisdom, Dries up the river of craving and perfectly teaches the Dharma.
examples.gm: For example, just as the rays of the sun dwelling in the sky Dry up this earth and also clearly reveal forms, Likewise, the dharma king, relying on the perfection of wisdom, Dries up the river of craving and also clearly reveals the dharma.
examples.sa: आकाशनिश्रित यथैव हि सूर्यरश्मि तापेतिमां धरणि दर्शयते च रूपम् । तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रित धर्मराजो तापेति तृष्णनदि धर्म निदर्शयाति ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: Those who engage in the practice of benefit and compassion, Having trained in this vidyā-mantra, the wise shall touch enlightenment; One should know that all forms of happiness, Whether conditioned or unconditioned, arise from this.
examples.gm: Those who practice the practices endowed with benefit and compassion, The wise ones, having trained in this mantra, will touch awakening. Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness, One should know that all those forms of happiness arise from this.
examples.sa: ये वा चरन्ति चरियां हितसानुकम्पाम् इह विद्यशिक्षित विदु स्पृशिष्यन्ति बोधिम् । ये सौख्य संस्कृत असंस्कृत ये च सौख्या सर्वे च सौख्य प्रसुता इतु वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: Teaching of the complete realization of all aspects
examples.gm: Teaching on the Clear Realization of All Aspects

examples.dm: The fourth chapter explains the complete realization of all aspects. Śakra, the king of the gods, asked the Victor: "How do Bodhisattvas practicing wisdom apply diligence?" "They do not apply even a particle of diligence toward the aggregates or the elements; Not applying diligence toward the aggregates is the Bodhisattva's diligence."
examples.gm: The fourth chapter: teaching the complete realization of all aspects. The king of gods, Śakra, asked the Victor: "How does a bodhisattva strive in the practice of wisdom?" "They do not strive even a speck of dust in the aggregates and elements; Not striving in the aggregates, that is the striving of a bodhisattva."
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनस्य परिपृच्छति देवराजो चरमाण प्रज्ञ कथ युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । अणुमात्र यो न खलु युज्यति स्कन्धधातौ यो एव युज्यति स युज्यति बोधिसत्त्वः ॥

examples.dm: They do not desire fame, and their minds are not entangled by anger. Even if they live as householders, they are always without attachment to any material things. For the sake of their livelihood, they do not seek out vast possessions. They do not practice wrathful spells of violence, nor do they practice spells for union with women.
examples.gm: Not desiring fame, their minds are not wrapped by anger. Even if they are householders, they are always unattached to all things. For the sake of livelihood, they do not seek resources through appalling means. They do not practice mantras of fierce actions, nor mantras for uniting men and women.
examples.sa: न च कीर्तिकाम न च क्रोधपरीतचित्ता गृहिभूत नित्य अनध्योषित सर्व वस्तुं । न च जीविकाविषयभोग गवेषयन्ति अभिचारमन्त्र न च इस्त्रिप्रयोगमन्त्राः ॥

examples.dm: It does not abide within the dharmadhātu or suchness; For example, like a cloud in the sky, it abides without a place to abide. A mantra-holder, a sky-traveler without a fixed abode, desiring a place to stay, Through the power of mantra, blesses trees to be endowed with out-of-season flowers.
examples.gm: They do not dwell in the dharmadhātu or suchness, For example, like clouds in space, they dwell without dwelling. A mantra-holder, without a dwelling, moving in space, wishing to dwell, By the power of mantras, is endowed with out-of-season flowers and blesses them.
examples.sa: न च धर्मधातुतथताय उपैति स्थानं भवती अथानस्थित सो लघु अन्तरीक्षे । विद्याधरो व अभिलम्भु वनाभिप्राया खगु कालहीन द्रुम मन्त्रबलाधिष्ठानो ॥

examples.dm: The many spirits and diseases in the human world Are pacified through the blessing of truth by those endowed with benefit and compassion; Yet they remain without conceit and do not give rise to pride— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In the human world, there are many bhūta demons and diseases; Possessing benefit and compassion, they pacify them through the blessing of truth. Yet they have no conceit and do not produce pride; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: भूतग्रहा विविध व्याधय मर्त्यलोके सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति हितानुकम्पी । न च तेन मन्यन् उपपद्यति नापि मानम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यः ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, the wise bodhisattva, having attained the fourfold tranquility Of concentration and meditative absorption that bestows joy and bliss, Relinquishes that blissful concentration and the meditative absorptions they have attained, And out of compassion for beings, enters again into the realm of desire.
examples.gm: Similarly, the wise bodhisattva, joy and Having attained the happiness-bestowing four peaceful samādhis of the dhyānas, Lets go of the attainment of the dhyāna samādhis endowed with the bliss of the dhyānas, And endowed with compassion for beings, again enters the desire realm.
examples.sa: एमेव ध्यान चतुर् एव समाधि शान्तां लब्ध्वान प्रीति सुखदां विदु बोधिसत्त्वाः । अवसृज्य ध्यानसुखप्रीतिसमाधिलाभं पुन कामधातु प्रविशन्ति जगानुकम्पी ॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, even though they are intensely engaged with the five sensory qualities— Forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures— If they take joy in the Bodhicitta that is free from the vehicles of the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, Know that these heroes are always in meditative equipoise.
examples.gm: Moreover, forms and sounds, and likewise smells and tastes, Touches, and the five qualities of desire, even if they exert themselves in these, If they are free from the vehicles of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening, The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: किंचापि रूपम् अपि शब्द तथैव गन्धो रस स्पर्श कामगुण पञ्चभि युक्त भोगी । रहप्रत्ययान विगतोऽनन्तबोधिसत्त्वो सततं समाहितु प्रजानयितव्य शूरो ॥

examples.dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: यदि पञ्च कामगुण भुञ्जति बोधिसत्त्वो बुद्धं च धर्म शरणागतु आर्यसंघम् । सर्वज्ञता च मनसी भविष्यामि बुद्धो स्थितु शीलपारमित वेदयितव्य विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: In the language of India: Ārya-prajñāpāramitā-sañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: 'Phags pa shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa sdud pa tshigs su bcad pa. Homage to the Noble Mañjuśrī!
examples.gm: In the language of India: Āryaprajñāpāramitāsañcayagāthā. In the language of Tibet: The Noble Verse Summary of the Perfection of Wisdom. Homage to the noble Mañjuśrī.
examples.sa: ओम् नमो भगवत्यै आर्यप्रज्ञापारमितारत्नगुणसंचयगाथायै । नमो आर्यमञ्जुश्रिये ।

examples.dm: Just as a wandering mendicant, through his knowledge of craftsmanship, Brings about the disintegration of the aggregates without any objective apprehension, Any bodhisattva who understands phenomena in that way, Does not touch nirvana, and is established in wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as the wanderer Śreṇika, through his knowledge, Understood the aggregates as unapprehendable and subject to destruction; Whatever bodhisattva understands phenomena in that way Does not contact nirvāṇa, and dwells in wisdom.
examples.sa: अथ श्रेणिकस्य अभुती परिव्राजकस्य ज्ञानोपलम्भु न हि स्कन्धविभावना च । यो बोधिसत्त्व परिजानति एव धर्मां न च निर्वृतिं स्पृशति सो विहराति प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: Form, perception, feeling, intention, And consciousness are neither bound nor freed, and they do not exist. Thus, entering into awakening without a discouraged mind, This is the supreme armor of holy beings.
examples.gm: Form and perception, feeling and volition, And consciousness are not bound, not liberated, and do not exist. Entering into awakening in this way, without a discouraged mind, This is the supreme armor of the noble persons.
examples.sa: रुपं च संज्ञ अपि वेदन चेतना च विज्ञान बन्धु न च मुक्त असङ्गभूतो । एवं च बोधि क्रमते न च लीनचित्तो संना ह एष वरपुद्गल-उत्तमानाम् ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: Suppose someone were to make offerings to the stūpas Of the Sugatas who have passed into parinirvāṇa, constructing them of the seven precious gems, And were to fill a thousand million buddha-fields With as many stūpas of the Sugatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges;
examples.gm: If someone, of the completely parinirvāṇized Sugata, Were to build stūpas from the seven precious things and make offerings, and with those stūpas of the Sugata, as numerous as the Ganges' Sands, were to fill thousands of millions of fields;
examples.sa: परिनिर्वृतस्य सुगतस्य करेय्य स्तूपां पूजेय सप्तरतनामयु कश्चिद् एव । तेहि प्रपूर्ण सिय क्षेत्रसहस्रकोट्यो यथ गङ्गवालिकसमैः सुगतस्य स्तूपैः ॥

examples.dm: Likewise, through the qualities of the supreme perfection of wisdom, The Victors receive worship of their relics even after they have passed into nirvana. Therefore, those who wish to grasp the qualities of the Victors Should take up this perfection of wisdom; it is liberation.
examples.gm: Likewise, through the qualities of the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even though the Victors pass into nirvana, their relics gain worship. Therefore, whoever wishes to hold the qualities of the Victors Should take up the perfection of wisdom; this is liberation.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमितागुणानि यन्निर्वृतेऽपि जिनधातु लभन्ति पूजाम् । तस्मा हु तान् जिनगुणा(न्) परिघेत्तुकामो सो प्रज्ञपारमित गृह्णतु एष मोक्षो ॥

examples.dm: From the time they first generate the aspiration for supreme enlightenment, Until the time the true Dharma of those guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors possess during that interval, Including the perfections and all the Buddha-qualities,
examples.gm: From when they first generated the mind for supreme awakening, Until the time the holy dharma of those Guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors have during that time, And whatever is endowed with the perfections and whatever buddha-dharmas—
examples.sa: प्रथमं उपादु वरबोधयि चित्तुपादो यावत् सु धर्मक्षयकालु विनायकानाम् । एकस्मि तत्र चिय तेष जिनान पुण्यं सह युक्त पारमित येऽपि च बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Even if one has honored billions of Buddhas in former lives, If one lacks faith in the Victors' perfection of wisdom, That person of small intelligence, upon hearing it, will reject it; Having rejected it, they become defenseless and go to the Unrelenting Hell.
examples.gm: Even if they honored hundreds of billions of buddhas when practicing previously, If they do not have faith in the perfection of wisdom of the Victors, Upon hearing it, those of small intelligence will abandon it; Having abandoned it, becoming without refuge, they go to the Avīci hell.
examples.sa: सत्कृत्य बुद्धनियुतां परिचारिकायां न च प्रज्ञपारमित श्रद्दधिता जिनानाम् । श्रुत्वा च सो इमु क्षिपिष्यति सोऽल्पबुद्धिः स क्षिपित्व यास्यति अवीचिम् अत्राणभूतो ॥

examples.dm: When a bodhisattva, through the perfection of wisdom, sees That all phenomena are naturally pure and utterly pristine, They do not perceive an agent, nor do they perceive any phenomena; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: All dharmas being naturally pure and entirely pure, If the bodhisattva views the perfection of wisdom, Not apprehending an agent and not apprehending all dharmas, This is practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: प्रकृतीय शुद्ध परिशुद्धिमि सर्वधर्मां प्रज्ञाय पारमित पश्यति बोधिसत्त्वो । न च पश्यकं लभति नापि च सर्वधर्मान् एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: They will desire honor and desire gain, And with a mind full of views, they will become intimate with householders; Abandoning the Dharma, they will engage in non-Dharmic activities— Leaving the path and wandering onto a wrong path, this is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: Desiring respect and desiring gain, With a mind full of views, they become intimate with families; Having forsaken the dharma, they will practice non-dharma activities; Having discarded the path, going on wrong paths—this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: सत्कारकाम भविष्यन्ति च लाभकामाः सापेक्षचित्त कुलसंस्तवसंप्रयुक्ताः । छोरित्व धर्म करिष्यन्ति अधर्मकार्यं पथ हित्व उत्पथगता इम मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: For example, just as a lion dwelling in a mountain glen is fearless, And its roar strikes terror into many small wild animals, So too the Lion among men, by relying on the Perfection of Wisdom, Terrifies the many non-Buddhists and lets out his roar throughout the world.
examples.gm: For example, just as a fearless lion dwelling in a mountain ravine Terrifies many small wild animals and lets out a roar, The lion of men, relying on the perfection of wisdom, Terrifies many tīrthikas and also lets out a roar in the world.
examples.sa: सिंहो यथैव गिरिकन्दरि निश्रयित्वा नदते अछम्भि मृग क्षुद्रक त्रासयन्तो । तथ प्रज्ञपारमितनिश्रय नराण सिंहो नदते अछम्भि पृथुतीर्थिक त्रासयन्तो ॥

examples.dm: For those bodhisattvas who abide on the level of a beginner, And have entered into the supreme awakening of a Buddha with a resolute intention, Those excellent students who possess devotion for their gurus Should always rely upon wise masters.
examples.gm: Any bodhisattva abiding on the ground of a beginner, Who has set out for the supreme enlightenment of a Buddha with a pure intention, As good disciples possessing devotion to their guru, They should always rely on wise gurus.
examples.sa: यो आदिकर्म स्थितु भूमिय बोधिसत्त्वो अध्याशयेन वर प्रस्थित बुद्धबोधिम् । तेही सुशिष्यगुरुगौरवसंप्रयुक्तो कल्याणमित्र सद सेवयितव्य विज्ञैः ॥

examples.dm: Those who possess such qualities are free from conceptual elaboration; Free from doubt, hesitation, and uncertainty, they are endowed with the true meaning. Having heard the perfection of wisdom, they do not shrink back; They do not rely on others and should be known as irreversible.
examples.gm: They are endowed with such dharmas and are free from conceptual proliferation. They are free from doubt, hesitation, and wavering, and possess the ultimate meaning. Those who, having heard the perfection of wisdom, do not shrink back, Should be known as irreversible and not reliant on others.
examples.sa: ते एव धर्मसमुदागत निष्प्रपञ्चा काङ्क्षाविलेखविमतीविगतार्थयुक्ताः । प्रज्ञाय पारमित श्रुत्व न सीदयन्ति अपरप्रणेय अविवर्तिय वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: They are free from the perception of diversity and speak words consistent with reason; They do not rely on other śramaṇas or brahmins. These wise ones have forever abandoned the three lower realms; They are intensely devoted to the paths of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.gm: Free from differentiated perceptions and speaking rational words, Not relying on other śramaṇas and brahmins; The wise always abandon the three lower realms at all times, And vividly strive in the path of the ten virtuous actions.
examples.sa: नानात्वसंज्ञविगता गिर युक्तभाणी न च अन्य ते श्रमण ब्राह्मण आश्रयन्ति । त्रियपायवर्जित विदू सदकालि भोन्ति दशभिश् च ते कुशलकर्मपथेभि युक्ता ॥

examples.dm: Knowing that all these dharmas, which the Buddha has thoroughly practiced and clearly taught, Are exhausted as mere expressions, Even if one were to speak of them for many tens of billions of eons, The expanse of phenomena is without exhaustion and without increase.
examples.gm: Spoken by the Buddha, vividly practiced and vividly taught, Knowing all these dharmas to be nothing more than mere expressions, Even if they are expressed for many tens of millions and hundreds of billions of eons, In the dharmadhātu, there is no depletion and no increase.
examples.sa: अभिलापमात्र इम जानति सर्वधर्मां बुद्धेन देशित प्रयुक्त प्रकाशितांश् च । कल्पान कोटिनयुतां बहु भाषमाणो न च क्षीयते न च विवर्धति धर्मधातुः ॥

examples.dm: The many spirits and diseases in the human world Are pacified through the blessing of truth by those endowed with benefit and compassion; Yet they remain without conceit and do not give rise to pride— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: In the human world, there are many bhūta demons and diseases; Possessing benefit and compassion, they pacify them through the blessing of truth. Yet they have no conceit and do not produce pride; They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: भूतग्रहा विविध व्याधय मर्त्यलोके सत्याधिष्ठानि प्रशमेति हितानुकम्पी । न च तेन मन्यन् उपपद्यति नापि मानम् अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यः ॥

examples.dm: For all the Victors of the past, the future, and those residing in the ten directions, This perfection is the path; there is no other. This perfection is said to be the clarity, the lamp, the light, And the supreme guide for those who have entered upon supreme enlightenment.
examples.gm: The Victorious Ones of the past, future, and whoever abide in the ten directions, The path of all of them is this perfection, and no other. This perfection is, for those entered into supreme awakening, Explained as the supreme illumination, lamp, light, and teacher.
examples.sa: अतिक्रान्तनागत जिना स्थित ये दिशासु सर्वेषु मार्गु अयु पारमिता अनन्यो । ओभास उल्क वरबोधयि प्रस्थितानाम् आलोक शास्त्रि इमि पारमिता प्रदिष्टाः ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who has long been connected to this, In order to liberate beings of the heavens, the human realm, and the three lower realms, And who desires to show the vast path to the realm of beings on the other side, Should day and night apply themselves to the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Any bodhisattva who, for the sake of liberating The sentient beings of gods, humans, and the three lower realms bound here for a long time, Desires to teach the broad path to the other shore to the realm of beings, Should strive in the perfection of wisdom day and night.
examples.sa: चिरबुद्धदेवमनुजान् त्रिअपायि सत्त्वान् परिमोचितुं य इह इच्छति बोधिसत्त्वो । पृथुमार्गु तीरु उपदर्शयि सत्त्वधातौ प्रज्ञाय पारमित युक्त दिवा च रात्रौ ॥

examples.dm: The Buddhas reached awakening through the perfection of patience; Generating mindfulness, thinking, "This mind of mine is not good," One should individually confess and restrain it for the future, And not take delight in it; that is how one trains in this Dharma of the Buddha.
examples.gm: "Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience." Generating mindfulness, thinking, "This mind is not good," Confessing individually and restraining themselves in the future, And not rejoicing, they train in this Dharma of the Buddhas.
examples.sa: अथ तस्युपद्यति मतीति अशोभना ति क्षान्तीय पारमित बोधि स्पृशन्ति बुद्धाः । प्रतिदर्शयाति पुन आयति संवराणि अपयाति वा स इह शिक्षति बुद्धधर्मे ॥

examples.dm: Those who have entered into the supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoice from the depths of their hearts in the generation of the mind of enlightenment; Though one might find the measure of the three thousandfold world system and Mount Meru by weighing them on a scale, The virtue of such rejoicing is not like that.
examples.gm: Regarding those who have fully entered supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoicing from the depths of one's heart in their generation of the mind— The Mount Meru of a trichiliocosm could be measured by weighing it on a scale, But the virtue of that rejoicing is not like that.
examples.sa: अविवर्तियस्य वरबोधयि प्रस्थितस्य यो चित्तुपादु अनुमोदितु आशयेन । त्रिसहस्र मेरु तुलयित्व सियाप्रमाणो न त्वेव तस्य कुशलस्यनुमोदनाये ॥

examples.dm: Just as a skilled carpenter creates mechanical figures of men and women That perform all kinds of tasks, Likewise, the bodhisattva who is skilled in the practice of wisdom Performs all activities through non-conceptual primordial awareness.
examples.gm: A wise carpenter crafts figures similar to Men and women, and they also perform all activities; Likewise, the wise bodhisattvas practicing wisdom Perform all activities with non-conceptualizing pristine awareness.
examples.sa: पलगण्ड दक्ष विदुना कृतु दारुयन्त्रो पुरुषे स्त्रितुल्य स करोति ह सर्वकार्यम् । एमेव प्रज्ञचरितो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो ज्ञानेन सर्व क्रिय कुर्वति निर्विकल्पो ॥

examples.dm: This is the supreme treasure of Dharma and the most excellent Dharma treasury; It is the Buddha lineage, the treasury of happiness and joy for all beings. The protectors of the world in the ten directions—those of the past and those yet to come— All arise from this, yet the expanse of reality is never exhausted.
examples.gm: This is the supreme Dharma-treasure and the holy Dharma-treasury; It is the lineage of the Buddhas, the treasury of happiness and joy of beings. The protectors of the world of the past, future, and the ten directions, Though they are born from this, the dharmadhātu does not become exhausted.
examples.sa: अग्रं निधान अयु उत्तमधर्मकोश बुद्धान गोत्रजननं सुखसौख्यगञ्जो । अतिक्रान्तनागत दशद्दिशि लोकनाथा इतु ते प्रसूत न च क्षीयति धर्मधातुः ॥

examples.dm: The great beings exist solely to bring sentient beings to maturity, To purify the fields, and to complete the perfections; They do not seek rebirth in the formless realm, thinking That the qualities of enlightenment and the perfections would thereby decline.
examples.gm: The great beings, to completely ripen sentient beings, Act only to purify the realms and complete the perfections; Thinking, "The qualities of awakening and the perfections will diminish," They do not seek birth in the formless realm.
examples.sa: अन्यत्र सत्त्वपरिपाचन क्षेत्रशोधी परिपूरणार्थ इमि पारमिता महात्मा । आरूप्यधातुउपपत्ति न प्रार्थयन्ती यत्रेह बोधिगुणपारमितान हानि ॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, even though they are intensely engaged with the five sensory qualities— Forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures— If they take joy in the Bodhicitta that is free from the vehicles of the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, Know that these heroes are always in meditative equipoise.
examples.gm: Moreover, forms and sounds, and likewise smells and tastes, Touches, and the five qualities of desire, even if they exert themselves in these, If they are free from the vehicles of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening, The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: किंचापि रूपम् अपि शब्द तथैव गन्धो रस स्पर्श कामगुण पञ्चभि युक्त भोगी । रहप्रत्ययान विगतोऽनन्तबोधिसत्त्वो सततं समाहितु प्रजानयितव्य शूरो ॥

examples.dm: If they should hear others speaking ill or using harsh words, The wise bodhisattva rejoices, thinking, "This is my happiness." Who speaks, who hears, who [speaks] to whom, and for what reason? One who possesses this supreme perfection of patience is wise.
examples.gm: If one hears abusive and harsh words from others, Thinking, "I am happy," the wise bodhisattva rejoices; Who speaks, who hears, by what, what is it, and for what reason? The wise one is endowed with the supreme perfection of patience.
examples.sa: परुषं श्रुणित्व वचनं परतो दुरुक्तं परितोषयाति सुसुखं विदु बोधिसत्त्वो । को भाषते क शृणुते कुतु कस्य केन सो युक्त क्षान्तिवरपारमिताय विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victors thinks, "These sentient beings are ethical, but those are unethical," Engaging in such diverse perceptions, they are utterly lacking in ethical discipline; Their morality has degenerated, and they lack completely purified morality.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victorious Ones Thinks, "These sentient beings have discipline; these have broken discipline," By engaging in such diverse perceptions, their discipline is completely broken; Their discipline degenerates, and they lack completely pure discipline.
examples.sa: यदि बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु जिनान मार्गे इमि शीलवानिमि दुशील करोति सत्त्वान् । नानात्वसंज्ञप्रसृतो परमं दुशीलो अपि छिद्रशीलु न तु सो परिशुद्धशीलो ॥

examples.dm: Those who grasp at the actual perception of a self and hold things as "mine" are attached; How could fools like these ever have the intention to give? Those who are stingy will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Even if they are born as humans, they will be destitute at that time.
examples.gm: Perceiving a self, one is attached to things through grasping them as "mine"; How could fools have the mind of generosity? Miserly ones will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts; Or even if they are born as humans, they will then be impoverished.
examples.sa: अहसंज्ञतस्तु ममता भवते च रागो कुतु त्यागबुद्धि भविष्यति सा मुहानाम् । मात्सर्य प्रेत भवते उपपद्ययाती अथवा मनुष्य तद भोति दरिद्ररूपो ॥

examples.dm: The sixth chapter explains the gradual path. Through the generosity of a bodhisattva, the path to the realm of hungry spirits is cut off; It likewise eliminates poverty and all afflictions. When practiced, one will obtain an infinite expansion of resources; Through generosity, one brings sentient beings who are suffering to full maturity.
examples.gm: Chapter Six: Teaching the Gradual Training. By the bodhisattva's giving, the destiny of hungry ghosts is cut off; Poverty and likewise all afflictions are cut off; While practicing, they will obtain infinite, abundant wealth, And by giving, they fully ripen sentient beings who are suffering.
examples.sa: दानेन प्रेतगति छिन्दति बोधिसत्त्वो दारिद्रकं च छिनती तथ सर्वक्लेशान् । भोगांश् चनन्तविपुलां लभते चरन्तो दानेन सत्त्व परिपाचयि कृच्छ्रप्राप्तान् ॥

examples.dm: The eighth chapter: teaching the Dharmakāya. One fully embraces the pure realm and the purity of sentient beings; One fully embraces the lineage of the Buddha and the lineage of the Dharma; Likewise, one fully embraces the lineage of the Saṅgha and all phenomena.
examples.gm: Chapter Eight: Teaching the Dharmakāya. Fully upholds perfectly pure fields and pure sentient beings; Fully upholds the Buddha lineage and also the Dharma lineage; Likewise fully upholds the Sangha lineage and all dharmas.
